Issues.Title: fix(forms): respect options passed as second argument to SignalFormControl
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When creating a `SignalFormControl` with options passed as the second argument (e.g. `new SignalFormControl(value, {injector})`), `SignalFormControl` forwards `[signal(value), schemaOrOptions, options]` to `normalizeFormArgs`.

Because a 3-element array is always passed, `normalizeFormArgs` takes its 3-argument branch, treating `schemaOrOptions` as the schema and `options` (which is `undefined`) as the options:
1. Outside an injection context, `opts?.injector` is `undefined`, causing `inject(Injector)` to be called and throw `NG0203` (`RuntimeError: NG0203: inject() must be called from an injection context`).
2. Inside an injection context, `inject(Injector)` succeeds, but `compatForm` forwards the options object as the schema to `form()`, which attempts to compile the options object as a schema function and throws `TypeError: this.schemaFn is not a function`.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

1. `normalizeFormArgs` trims trailing `undefined` arguments and checks `isSchemaOrSchemaFn` when 3 arguments are provided, correctly routing options into `options` when the second argument is not a schema.
2. `SignalFormControl` normalizes arguments first, uses the normalized options for `updateOn` validation, and forwards the injector and form options to `compatForm`.
3. `new SignalFormControl(value, {injector})` works correctly both outside and inside an injection context, and other options (such as `name`) are preserved.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Issues.Title: fix(forms): preserve options passed to SignalFormControl
Issues.Body:
Ensure that options passed to `SignalFormControl` (either as the second argument or as the third argument with a schema or `undefined`) are preserved and correctly forwarded to `compatForm` and `form()`.

Previously:
- `normalizeFormArgs` relied on `args.length === 3`, causing options passed as the second argument (e.g. `new SignalFormControl(value, {name: 'foo', injector})`) to be misidentified as a schema function.
- `SignalFormControl` only forwarded `{injector}` to `compatForm`, discarding any other options such as `name`.

This PR:
- Updates `normalizeFormArgs` to check `isSchemaOrSchemaFn(args[1])` rather than relying on argument count.
- Adds constructor overloads to `SignalFormControl` for schema or options as the second argument.
- Ensures all options are preserved and forwarded to `compatForm`.
- Adds comprehensive unit tests for `normalizeFormArgs` and `SignalFormControl` options handling.

Issues.Title: fix(forms): isolate debounce abort listeners from reactive tracking
Issues.Body:
## What changes

Abort listeners currently run inside the `pendingSync` linked-signal computation. Signal writes throw even in production, and reads become accidental dependencies that can cause a later typed value to be discarded. A completed debounce also retains its controller and gets aborted on a later touch.

Run listeners untracked and clear the controller when its debounce completes. Check orphaned/aborted/superseded state before reading pending state after the await.

Related to #71631. This deliberately keeps the linked signal and the existing lazy cancellation timing after direct model writes; it does not introduce an effect per field or promise eager cancellation. Public API signatures are unchanged.

## Reproduction and production results

The three regression specs in this PR fail on main at `2d12a5e8f457f183545fa14364b6f8982ec21452` and pass with the fix.

The same cases were independently run in an AOT, ES2022, minified browser fixture built from that base and the patched source, with `ngDevMode=false`, `ngJitMode=false`, and runtime `isDevMode() === false`. It exercises public `controlValue.set()` and `markAsTouched()` field APIs.

| Production scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complete debounce, then touch | 1 unnecessary abort | 0 aborts |
| Abort listener writes a signal after a direct model update | 1 error; indicator stays true | no error; indicator false |
| Earlier abort listener reads an unrelated signal, then it changes | model keeps `direct`, losing `second` | model contains `second` |

## Cost and memory comparison

Seven alternating baseline/patched pairs, fresh browser contexts, Chromium 158.0.8117.0 on Linux x64. One live form, 100 warmup edits, followed by two batches of 1000 completed edit/touch cycles. Heap readings follow three forced GCs.

| Median, per 1000-cycle batch | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unnecessary abort callbacks | 1000 | 0 |
| Time, second batch | 14.5 ms | 5.9 ms |
| Heap increase, first batch | 132,672 bytes | 134,728 bytes |
| Further heap increase, second batch | 5,736 bytes | 1,016 bytes |

Timing ranges for the second batch: 11.0–17.6 ms before, 3.8–10.1 ms after. These are microbenchmark totals, not page-latency guarantees.

**An unbounded memory leak was not established by this experiment.** Both heaps largely plateau after warmup; no substantial memory-saving claim is made. The demonstrated production impact is lost input, failed signal writes, and redundant cancellation work.

## Validation

- Node: 556 specs, 0 failures.
- Chromium: 362 specs, 0 failures, including existing removed-field/orphan coverage.
- ng-dev format and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local browser-test infrastructure needed a loopback fallback only when this container rejects `os.networkInterfaces()`; no Angular/test assertions were changed. Bazel telemetry was disabled.

[angular-71631-production-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34282158/angular-71631-production-repro.zip)

Issues.Title: Unguarded Map access and leaked PendingTask in triggerHydrationForBlockQueue
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

`triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` in `packages/core/src/defer/triggering.ts` reads an entry from `DehydratedBlockRegistry.hydrating` without a guard, after two `await` points during which that entry can be removed.

The same Map is read three times in that function. Two of the three reads are optional-chained, one is not:

```ts
blocksBeingHydrated.get(dehydratedBlockId).resolve();   // unguarded
await blocksBeingHydrated.get(lastBlockName)?.promise;  // guarded
blocksBeingHydrated.get(dehydratedBlockId)?.reject();   // guarded
```

`DehydratedBlockRegistry.cleanup()` does `this.hydrating.delete(blockId)`, so the entry is genuinely removable while the function is suspended on `await triggerResourceLoadingForHydration()` or `await nextRender()`.

### Second defect in the same function

`pendingTasks.add()` runs at the top and `pendingTasks.remove(taskId)` further down, with no `try/finally` between them. When the unguarded access throws, the task is never released. `PendingTasksInternal` has no timeout, so `ApplicationRef.isStable` never becomes true again for that session, and anything gated on `whenStable()` or `isStable` silently stops working for the rest of the session.

Every caller of `triggerHydrationFromBlockName` is fire-and-forget, with no `await` and no `.catch()`, so the failure surfaces only as an unhandled rejection with no application frame in the stack.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

We could not build one, and we want to be upfront about that.

We built a minimal SSR app on 22.2.3 with `withIncrementalHydration()` and a `@defer (hydrate on idle)` under an `@if`, held the deferred chunk through network interception to widen the window, and destroyed the host view at several points. Six scenarios, including nested hydrate blocks, produced no error.

We believe this is because `ɵɵdefer` registers `storeTriggerCleanupFn(0, lDetails, () => removeLViewOnDestroy(lView, onLViewDestroy))`, so the destroy hook that would call `registry.cleanup()` is removed as soon as the block triggers. Something else removes the entry, and we have not identified it.

We are reporting this as a code defect rather than a reproducible behaviour: the missing `?.` and the missing `try/finally` are visible by inspection, and both fixes are small and independent of whatever triggers the removal.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'resolve')    // Chrome
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'o.get(p).resolve') // Safari
TypeError: can't access property "resolve", o.get(...) is undefined   // Firefox
```

The throwing line is `packages/core/src/defer/triggering.ts:478`.

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in

Angular 22.2.3, SSR with incremental hydration, zoneless change detection. Chrome, Safari and Firefox, on desktop and mobile.

### Anything else?

Suggested fixes, both independent of the unknown trigger:

1. Optional-chain the read at `triggering.ts:478`, matching the two sibling reads in the same function.
2. Wrap the body of `triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` in `try/finally` so `pendingTasks.remove(taskId)` always runs.

The second one matters more than the error itself: a leaked pending task permanently breaks application stability for the rest of the session.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Unguarded Map access and leaked PendingTask in triggerHydrationForBlockQueue" (#71769)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): keep leading colon of attribute names instead of parsing it as a namespace separator
Issues.Body:
Previously, an attribute name starting with a colon (e.g. `<button :disabled="xxxx">`) was parsed as a namespace with an empty prefix, silently dropping the colon and turning the attribute into `disabled`, which disabled the button. This diverges from plain HTML, where `:disabled` is an attribute literally named `:disabled` with no effect on the `disabled` property.

The lexer now only treats a colon as a namespace separator in attribute names when it is preceded by a non-empty prefix, so a leading colon stays part of the attribute name, matching the plain HTML behavior.

Fixes #44185

Issues.Title: fix(core): cancel obsolete resource loads when params become unavailable
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

When params return `undefined`, propagate `ResourceParamsStatus.IDLE`/`LOADING`, or throw an error during a pending load, `loadEffect()` returns before cancelling the obsolete loader. The resource changes status, but the old AbortSignal stays active and its pending task can block application stability indefinitely.

Fixes #71765.

## What is the new behavior?

Cancel the previous load before checking whether the new request can run. Unavailable params now abort obsolete work and release its pending task, including when the old loader never settles.

Add six regressions covering undefined params, propagated statuses/errors, recovery, and late resolution/rejection after a new load starts. The latter checks that old completions neither replace the new state nor release the new load's pending task.

Validation:

Issues.Title: fix(core): preserve generic type parameters when injecting or querying tokens
Issues.Body:
In TypeScript, instantiation expressions on class constructors (such as `ElementRef<HTMLElement>`) only specialize construct signatures (`new`), leaving the `prototype` property unspecialized (e.g. `ElementRef<any>`). Because `ProviderToken<T>` is a union that includes `AbstractType<T>` (`{ prototype: T }`), passing `ElementRef<HTMLElement>` to `inject()`, `Injector.get()`, or signal queries (`viewChild`, `viewChildren`, `contentChild`, `contentChildren`) caused TypeScript to infer `T` from `prototype`, widening the return type to `ElementRef<any>`.

Rather than changing `AbstractType<T>` (which would cause broad type regressions across existing code), this change introduces an internal `InjectClassResult<C>` helper type along with prioritized overloads on `Type<unknown>` and `abstract new (...args: any[]) => T` for:
- `inject()`
- `Injector.get()`
- Signal queries (`viewChild`, `viewChild.required`, `viewChildren`, `contentChild`, `contentChild.required`, `contentChildren`) for both locator tokens and `read` options.

`InjectClassResult<C>` inspects constructor parameters of `C`. When parameters are unspecialized (`unknown` / `any`, as in `ElementRef`), it defaults to the prototype type (`ElementRef<any>`), while preserving the specialized instance type when generic arguments are explicitly provided (e.g. `ElementRef<HTMLButtonElement>`).

Fixes #53894
Fixes #48126

Issues.Title: feat(compiler-cli): add opt-in diagnostic for unstable @for track keys
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the [commit message guidelines](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md).
- [x] Tests have been added.
- [x] Documentation has been added and updated.

## PR Type

- [x] Feature

## What is the current behavior?

Object and array literals are valid in `@for` tracking expressions, but each evaluation creates a new reference. Existing diagnostics do not identify these expressions at compile time:

```html
@for (user of users(); track {id: user.id}) {}
@for (user of users(); track [user.id]) {}
```

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

Add NG8120 (`unstableTrackExpression`) for direct object and array literals, including parenthesized expressions. The diagnostic points to the tracking expression and recommends a stable key such as `user.id`.

Property access, primitive keys, `$index`, stable object references, function calls, and Signal Forms field identities remain accepted. The check does not analyze conditional expressions or function implementations. It is also implemented in the NGP preprocessor.

The check is opt-in through the existing configuration:

```json
{
  "angularCompilerOptions": {
    "strictTemplates": true,
    "extendedDiagnostics": {
      "checks": {
        "unstableTrackExpression": "warning"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

An explicit `warning` or `error` entry is required. `suppress` disables the check. `defaultCategory` alone does not enable it, including when set to `error`. The existing factory options hook provides this behavior without adding configuration fields or changing the shared category-resolution logic.

Documentation describes stable tracking keys, configuration, and the relationship to NG0955, NG0956, and NG8115.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Template grammar, AST contracts, generated instructions, runtime reconciliation, existing diagnostic behavior, and existing API signatures are preserved. The diagnostic name is added to the existing configuration enum and its API golden is updated. Projects that have not opted in retain their compilation behavior, including those using `defaultCategory: "error"`.

## Other information

Validation: all 43 affected Bazel targets pass:

| Suite | Passed | Pre-existing pending |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Compiler unit tests | 1,770 | 14 |
| Extended Diagnostics: ngtsc | 1,457 | 0 |
| Extended Diagnostics: NGP | 1,064 | 328 |
| ngtsc integration: extended diagnostics and template type-checking | 1,552 | 8 |
| NGP integration: new unstable-track cases | 76 | 0 |
| **Total** | **5,919** | **350** |

The new unit suite passes 128/128 on both ngtsc and NGP. All 76 new integration cases pass on each backend. Coverage includes inline/external templates, exact source spans, parentheses, accepted stable keys, nested loops, Signal Forms identity, categories, strict-template requirements, NG8115 coexistence, unchanged default compilation, and identical emitted JavaScript.

The NGP test bridge now forwards explicit categories for selected factories, allowing opt-in checks to run. Existing assertions and known-failure lists are unchanged.

TypeScript type-checking, typed TSLint, Prettier, Buildifier, and `git diff --check` pass. A diagnostic-only microbenchmark visits 10,000 stable loops in approximately 22 ms median; unconfigured projects create no additional template-check pass.

Issues.Title: docs(service-worker): clarify how applicationMaxAge is measured
Issues.Body:
The applicationMaxAge docs and schema description read as if the age were counted from when files were cached on the device. The service worker actually compares the age against the manifest timestamp, which is set when ngsw.json is generated at build time.

Once the build is older than applicationMaxAge, every request bypasses the cache and goes to the network, even when no newer version has been deployed, so the application does not work offline until a new build is deployed. When the property is omitted, there is no maximum age.

Update the guide and the JSON schema description to state this.

The format check requires every touched file to be formatted, so this also formats `schema.json`, which was not formatted on main.

Fixes #71720

Issues.Title: fix(core): allow binding null and undefined to resource URL properties
Issues.Body:
Binding `null` or `undefined` to a resource URL property such as `<iframe [src]>` throws NG0904 ("unsafe value used in a resource URL context"), even though there is nothing unsafe about clearing the binding. The inlined `ɵɵsanitizeResourceUrl` only accepts values marked trusted with `bypassSecurityTrustResourceUrl` and rejects everything else, including nullish values. This forces users to bind a trusted placeholder such as `about:blank` instead of simply using `undefined`.

The same binding already works when a custom `Sanitizer` is provided, because `DomSanitizer.sanitize` returns `null` for nullish values, which is then mapped to an empty string. Apply the same handling to the inlined sanitizer: `null` and `undefined` are mapped to an empty string, which the browser treats as `about:blank` for `<iframe src>`. Since `setElementAttribute` runs the sanitizer before removing an attribute for a nullish value, this also fixes `[attr.src]` bindings on resource URL attributes.

Fixes #42527

## What is the current behavior?

Binding `null` or `undefined` to a resource URL property throws at runtime:


The inlined `ɵɵsanitizeResourceUrl` only accepts values marked trusted with `bypassSecurityTrustResourceUrl` and rejects everything else, including nullish values. The same binding already works when a custom `Sanitizer` is provided in the injector, because `DomSanitizer.sanitize` returns `null` for nullish values, which is then mapped to an empty string. The two code paths are inconsistent.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): validate dist-tags and manifest caching under modern yarn
Issues.Body:
Modern yarn (`yarn npm info`) silently falls back to the `latest` version with exit code 0 not
only when a requested SemVer version or range is unmet, but also when a requested dist-tag does
not exist. Previously, `getRegistryManifest` only checked valid SemVer ranges, allowing unknown
dist-tags to resolve to `latest`.

Include `dist-tags` in modern yarn's requested `--fields` and add `parseYarnModernManifest` to
verify that non-range version specifiers exist in `dist-tags` and resolve to the returned
manifest version before stripping `dist-tags` from the result.

Move the SemVer range validation inside `#fetchAndParse`'s parser callback so rejected fallback
manifests are cached directly as `null` rather than storing the mismatched manifest object, and
scope `includePrerelease` to wildcard (`*`) specifiers so unmet major or x-ranges do not accept
prerelease `latest` fallbacks.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): enable oxc WASI fallback in WebContainer environments (22.2.x)
Issues.Body:
In WebContainer environments (such as StackBlitz and angular.dev playground), native Node.js addons cannot run, requiring oxc-parser to fall back to WebAssembly (WASI).

However, `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.156.0` specifies `@emnapi/core@2.0.0-alpha.6` while depending on `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime@~1.2.6` (which was updated for `@emnapi/core@>=2.0.0-beta.2`). In wasm-runtime 1.2.6, `initWorker` is assigned to `emnapi_shared.addonModule`, which is undefined in alpha.6 (where it was named `napiModule`), throwing `TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'initWorker')`.

This PR introduces `oxc-wasi-shim`, which aliases `addonModule` to `this.napiModule` on `Object.prototype` when running in WebContainer or when `NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI` is enabled, allowing the WASI runtime to initialize successfully. In addition, `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` is removed from `optionalDependencies` since oxc-parser's built-in WebContainer fallback downloads and loads it on demand.

An end-to-end test verifying `ng serve` with `NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI=true` is also included.

Backport of #34628
Fixes #34524

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): use oxc-parser fallback when stripping source-map comments
Issues.Body:
Previously, `removeSourceMappingURL` relied on a custom character-by-character state machine to strip top-level `//# sourceMappingURL=` comments from JavaScript strings. Because that scanner did not track regular expression literals, quote characters or backticks inside a regex literal (such as `/"/`) inverted string boundaries for the remainder of the file. When a subsequent string literal contained `//# sourceMappingURL=`, the scanner misidentified it as a top-level comment and truncated valid JavaScript, or failed to strip the actual trailing comment at the end of the chunk.

Extend the single-trailing-comment fast path to string inputs and pass raw byte buffers directly from the Vite memory plugin so standard chunks slice trailing source-map comments without invoking a parser. When a file contains multiple or non-trailing `//# sourceMappingURL=` occurrences, lazily load `oxc-parser` and read only the `comments` of the parse result, avoiding JS-side AST deserialization while delegating full ECMAScript lexical handling (including regex literals, templates, and escapes) to Oxc. This keeps main-thread startup free of eager native or WASM parser loading. The fallback removes whitespace consistently with the fast path, removing comment-only lines entirely while preserving line terminators for comments that follow code. Also harden trailing URL and base64 validation so block comments or template literals closing on the same line are never misclassified by the fast path.

Closes #34590

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): fall back to Babel linker in WebContainer environments
Issues.Body:
### Description

PR #34540 added `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` as an optional dependency to `@angular/build` to avoid runtime package manager execution in WebContainer environments. However, the playground and StackBlitz continue to fail.

#### Root Cause Analysis

1. **Upstream NAPI-RS / Emnapi Version Mismatch ([napi-rs/napi-rs#3674](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/issues/3674)):**
   Published `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` releases depend on `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime: ~1.2.x`, which resolves to `1.2.6`. However, `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime@1.2.6` declares peer dependencies of `@emnapi/core: ^1.7.1 || 2.0.0-beta.2`, which rejects the `@emnapi/core@2.0.0-alpha.x` that the WASI binding was built against.
   Package managers therefore install an isolated `@emnapi/core@1.11.3` beneath `wasm-runtime`, while the binding initializes its context using `@emnapi/runtime@2.0.0-alpha.x`. Calling `createEnv()` between these mismatched major versions throws a fatal runtime error:
   ```text
   TypeError: this.bridge.setLastError is not a function
   ```
2. **WebContainer Fallback Failure:**
   When loading `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` throws this error, `oxc-parser`'s `bindings.js` falls back to `webcontainer-fallback.cjs`, which attempts to shell out to `childProcess.execFileSync('pnpm', ['i', ...], { cwd: '/tmp/...' })` synchronously from inside a Piscina worker thread. This execution fails (and would install the same broken WASI version anyway), which Node.js's synchronous `require(esm)` loader reports as:
   ```text
   Error [ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE]: Cannot require() ES Module .../oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle.
   ```
3. **Eager Worker Module Initialization:**
   `javascript-transformer-worker.ts` had a top-level eager import `import { transform as transformWithOxc } from '../oxc/oxc-transform.js'`. Even in development (`ng serve`), where `advancedOptimizations` is false, the worker thread crashed on startup before handling any requests.

#### Proposed Solution

Mirror the existing WebContainer detection pattern used for `useSassEmbedded` (`!process.versions.webcontainer`):
1. **Default `useBabelLinker` to `true` in WebContainer:** In WebContainer environments (`process.versions.webcontainer`), default `useBabelLinker` to `true` (while still allowing explicit override via `NG_BUILD_BABEL_LINKER`). The Babel linker is pure JavaScript and has zero native or WASI dependencies.
2. **Lazy-load `oxc-transform`:** Remove the top-level eager import of `oxc-transform.js` in `javascript-transformer-worker.ts` so workers boot without evaluating `oxc-parser`.
3. **Graceful Fallback:** Skip attempting OXC in WebContainer (unless explicitly requested via `NG_BUILD_BABEL_LINKER=false`), and gracefully fall back to the Babel linker if OXC fails to load.

Fixes #34524

### Command

### Description

When I create a new project with `ng new --package-manager pnpm` on pnpm 11 or later, `ng new` itself works, but the next `pnpm add` fails. A fresh `pnpm install` (after a clone, or on CI) fails the same way.

`@angular/build` depends on `esbuild`, `@parcel/watcher` and `lmdb` (which brings in `msgpackr-extract`), and they all have install scripts. Since pnpm 11, `strictDepBuilds` is on by default, so pnpm fails the install unless each of them is approved or denied under `allowBuilds` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. `ng new` doesn't hit it because it installs with `--ignore-scripts`, so it only shows up afterwards.

I ran into this in my project: https://github.com/Blotch-Smart-Frames/AngularLynx/issues/188

I have worked around it in my own `ng add` schematic, but every pnpm user gets this from a plain `ng new`, so I think `ng new` should write the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` for pnpm projects.

### Minimal Reproduction

```
npx @angular/cli@22.2.5 new repro --package-manager pnpm --defaults
cd repro
pnpm add date-fns
```

A fresh install fails too:

```
rm -rf node_modules
pnpm install
```

### Exception or Error

```text
Error: ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS

  × adding a new package
  ╰─▶ Ignored build scripts: @parcel/watcher@2.6.0, esbuild@0.28.2,
      lmdb@3.5.6, msgpackr-extract@3.0.4
  help: Run "pnpm approve-builds" to pick which dependencies should be allowed
        to run scripts.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.5
Angular           : 22.2.4
Node.js           : 24.22.0
Package Manager   : pnpm 12.16.1
Operating System  : darwin arm64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.5           │
│ @angular/cli              │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.5           │
│ @angular/common           │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/core             │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/forms            │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/router           │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ~7.8.0            │
│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
│ vitest                    │ 5.0.5             │ ^5.0.0            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else relevant?

On pnpm 10 it's only a warning, so it works there.

Adding this `pnpm-workspace.yaml` to the new project fixes it. `pnpm install`, `pnpm add` and `ng build` all work after. It's the same as what this repo has in its own `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  '@parcel/watcher': false
  esbuild: false
  lmdb: false
  msgpackr-extract: false
```

One thing to watch out for: pnpm older than 10.26 doesn't read `allowBuilds`, and pnpm 9 and 10.0 fail on a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` that has no `packages` field. So it probably needs a pnpm version check.

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

<!-- Please check all that apply using "x". -->

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Errors thrown while `applyContentTemplate` renders a file don't say which file. With a misspelled variable, `ng generate` prints only `foobat is not defined`. A syntax error inside `<% %>` prints `Unexpected identifier 'unintended'`. In both cases the stack points only into `@angular-devkit/core`.

There is a related bug in the same `try` block. Since 18.1.0 (41ee8eac1), the `catch` returns the entry unchanged for any `TypeError`, so that content that isn't valid UTF-8 is left alone. Because decoding and rendering share that `try`, a `TypeError` thrown by the template itself is also ignored, for example `<%= name.length %>` with `name` undefined. The schematic then succeeds and writes the unrendered template.

Issue Number: #13192

## What is the new behavior?

The PR has two commits.

1. **Decode and render separately.** Content that can't be decoded is still returned unchanged. A `TypeError` from the template is now reported, as it was before 18.1.0.
2. **Name the template.** An error from rendering is rethrown with the template path, keeping the original error as `cause`, like `HostTree`'s `Failed to decode "<path>"` error. With a template at `files/sub/__name__.ts.template` applied through `url('./files')`, the message is:

```
Failed to apply content template to "/sub/__name__.ts.template": foobat is not defined
```

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

## Other information

**Tests.** The specs in `template_spec.ts` cover:
- a `TypeError` thrown by a template;
- content that isn't valid UTF-8, which is still returned unchanged;
- a `ReferenceError` and a `SyntaxError`, checking the message and the `cause`;
- an `applyTemplates` case that checks the path in the message.

I ran them with jasmine and tsx, outside Bazel. Each commit's new specs fail without its change and pass with it.

**Other suites.** All 141 specs under `packages/angular_devkit/schematics` pass, except two `FileSystemEngineHost` specs that need a Bazel-built fixture; they fail the same way on `main`.

**Built-in templates.** Because template TypeErrors used to be ignored, I also ran the 930 `@schematics/angular` specs on `main` and on this branch. I generated the schema `.ts` files with `tools/quicktype_runner.js` first. The same 18 specs fail on both in this Windows setup, so none of the built-in templates relied on the old behaviour.

**Checks.** `tsc` 6.0.3 and prettier are clean for the changed files.

**Side effects.** A `SchematicsException` thrown on purpose by a template helper is now wrapped the same way. Its message still appears after the path, and the exception itself is kept as `cause`.

**Not covered.** The message doesn't include the line inside the template, because the template is compiled with `Function()` and its line numbers don't match the template's.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): strip terminal escape sequences in modern yarn error parser
Issues.Body:
Modern Yarn formats error detail fields such as `Response Code` with ANSI color sequences and OSC 8 hyperlinks before passing them to `StreamReport`, which serializes the formatted strings verbatim into its JSON line output. When colors are enabled, such as by default on GitHub Actions even over non-TTY pipes or via `FORCE_COLOR` and `.yarnrc.yml` settings, escape codes appear around both the `Response Code` label and status number. As a result, `parseYarnModernError` failed to match the HTTP status code, fell back to the generic `YN0035` code instead of `E404` for missing packages, and leaked raw control sequences into the parsed summary and detail text.

Strip VT control characters from modern Yarn error messages prior to matching an anchored `Response Code` line, and ignore 2xx status codes for consistency with the Yarn Classic parser. In addition, split multi-line error payloads such as `YN0001` exception stack traces so `summary` only retains the first line while remaining lines move into `detail`, fall back to `UNKNOWN_ERROR` when `displayName` is an empty string (when `enableMessageNames` is disabled), and return `null` directly when no JSON error lines are present instead of delegating to `parseNpmLikeError` on every successful command output.

Issues.Title: bug(MatSlider): showTickMarks can exhaust memory during SSR
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`ngAfterViewInit()` measures the slider only in the browser, but it builds the tick marks on the server too:

```ts
if (this._platform.isBrowser) {
  this._updateDimensions();
}
// ...
this._updateTickMarkUI();
```

`_updateTickMarkUINonRange()` allocates one entry per tick mark:

```ts
this._tickMarks = Array(numActive)
  .fill(_MatTickMark.ACTIVE)
  .concat(Array(numInactive).fill(_MatTickMark.INACTIVE));
```

The template only renders them `@if (_cachedWidth)`, and the server never sets `_cachedWidth`. So during SSR the array is built and thrown away, and nothing bounds its size: it is `(max - min) / step`.

A slider whose bounds come from the URL is enough:

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'price-range',
  imports: [MatSliderModule],
  template: `
    <mat-slider [min]="min" [max]="max" [step]="step" showTickMarks>
      <input matSliderThumb />
    </mat-slider>
  `,
})
export class PriceRange {
  private readonly params = inject(ActivatedRoute).snapshot.queryParamMap;
  readonly min = Number(this.params.get('min') ?? '0');
  readonly max = Number(this.params.get('max') ?? '100');
  readonly step = Number(this.params.get('step') ?? '1');
}
```

I served it with `RenderMode.Server` and compared `/?max=1e9` with a control of the same size, `/?max=1e2`. Each cell is three fresh workers, and `fatal` means a V8 `FATAL ERROR` with exit code 134:

| Heap                | `?max=1e2` | `?max=1e9`           |
| ------------------- | ---------- | -------------------- |
| 256 MiB             | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 3.0 s |
| 1 GiB               | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.5 s |
| 4 GiB               | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.8 s |
| 16 GiB              | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.6 s |
| default (4,288 MiB) | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.6 s |

A bigger heap doesn't help. Above 2^25 entries `Array(n)` switches to dictionary elements, and from about 2.5e8 entries the dictionary hits V8's hash table limit before the heap fills up:

```text
FATAL ERROR: invalid table size Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

`?min=-1e9` and `?step=1e-7` also reach a billion tick marks and are fatal too. The values don't need to look odd either: `?max=1000000&step=0.01`, a price with cents, is 1e8 tick marks and kills a 512 MiB worker.

#26322 fixed #26317 by skipping the array when `showTickMarks` is off. With it on, the count is still unbounded, and #29496 is the browser side of the same problem. #33242 rewrites the method as a `push` loop over `Math.floor((max - min) / step) + 1`, so the count doesn't change. I applied it on top of 22.2.5: `?max=1e9` still kills a 256 MiB worker, `?max=3e7` now does too, and `?step=1e-309` goes from an immediate `RangeError` to a fatal error.

Returning early from `_updateTickMarkUI()` until `_cachedWidth` is set, which the template already requires, makes every request above return 200. The browser still builds the full array once the slider has a width.


As a note I found this while adapting `MatSlider` for a design system, using its code as the base. In an e-commerce app, passing the price filter's value or range through query parameters could OOM the SSR worker, so I would think this is a normal real use case.


### Reproduction

See  https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-material-slider-ssr-oom

Steps to reproduce:

1. `npm ci && npm run build`
2. `npm run serve:ssr:srr-material-oom`
3. `curl "http://localhost:4000/?max=1e9"`


### Expected Behavior

The server renders the slider without building tick marks it can't render, and the worker keeps serving other requests.


### Actual Behavior

The SSR worker aborts with a V8 fatal error (exit code 134), and every request in flight on it fails with it.


### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4, `@angular/ssr` 22.2.5, Node.js 24.16.0 (also 21.2.25 and 20.3.34)
- CDK/Material: 22.2.5 (also 21.2.14 and 20.2.14). `main` and 22.3.0-next.4 have the same code.
- Browser(s): n/a, server-side rendering
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Windows 11 x64

Issues.Title: fix(material/slider): prevent out of memory errors from tick marks on…
Issues.Body:
The slider only renders its tick marks once it has a width, but it was computing them regardless, allocating one array entry per tick mark. Since the number of entries is derived from the `min`, `max`, `step` and value, a large range or a small step could result in an array big enough to exhaust the heap. This was especially problematic during server-side rendering, because the slider never has a width on the server so the array was always built and then discarded. If any of those inputs are derived from user input (e.g. query parameters), a single request could crash the server process along with every other request it was handling.

These changes skip computing the tick marks until the slider has a width.

Fixes #34036

Issues.Title: fix(material/select): prevent option selection while disabled
Issues.Body:
## Problem

1. Open an enabled `mat-select`.
2. Disable it while its panel is open (for example, when an asynchronous request completes).
3. Click an option in the open panel. The selected value changes and `selectionChange` fires.

In Chromium I observed a native HTML select close its popup when disabled. The [HTML option-picking algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#concept-select-pick) also stops when the select is disabled.

I investigated this interaction while using Hegel to vary component props and Bombadil to exercise UI actions in Anta, then reproduced the Angular Material behavior independently with Playwright.

## Change

Prevent user interactions with options when the parent select is disabled. This preserves the panel's current open state and leaves programmatic value changes available. Option styling and ARIA attributes are unchanged; feedback on the preferred disabled presentation is welcome.

## Validation

- Confirmed the new regression fails on unmodified source in Chromium and Firefox.
- `pnpm exec bazel test //src/material/select:unit_tests --test_output=errors` passes in Chromium and Firefox with the change.


## Reproduction video

Recorded before the fix with Angular Material 21.2.14, the official Azure Blue prebuilt theme, and a standard `mat-form-field`. Click "Disable in 3 seconds", open the select, wait for the field to turn gray, then click Orange. The parent select is disabled; the individual options are enabled. The click changes the value and emits `selectionChange`. No forced click or custom select/option/overlay styles are used.

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/dialog): aria-hidden not restored when dialogs from parent and child are closed
Issues.Body:
When a `Dialog` is provided at the component level, it shares its list of open dialogs with the
parent `Dialog`, but each instance tracked the elements it hid with `aria-hidden` separately.
Opening a dialog from a child `Dialog` and then one from the parent (or vice versa) meant that the
instance closing the last dialog had nothing to restore, so `aria-hidden` stayed on the page
content after all dialogs were closed, leaving the app inaccessible to assistive technology.

This change shares the map of hidden elements with the parent `Dialog`, following the same
pattern already used for `openDialogs` and `afterAllClosed`. A unit test covering the
parent/child scenario was added; it fails without the fix.

Fixes #30028
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(cdk/dialog): aria-hidden not restored when dialogs from parent and child are closed" (#34043)

Issues.Title: fix(material/input): input harness not dispatching change event
Issues.Body:
`MatInputHarness.setValue` updates the value by clearing the input, sending keys and setting the
value property, but it never dispatches a `change` event. As a result, `(change)` listeners on a
`matInput` aren't invoked in tests, even though the value changed (see the reproduction in the issue).

This change dispatches a `change` event at the end of `setValue`, which is consistent with what
`MatDatepickerInputHarness.setValue` already does (#20877). A unit test was added that fails without
the fix.

Fixes #30160
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/input): input harness not dispatching change event" (#34042)

Issues.Title: docs: keep anchored headings clear of the sticky section tabs
Issues.Body: ## Summary Anchor targets on component pages scroll underneath the sticky Overview/API/Styling/Examples tab nav. This gives them a `scroll-margin-top` so they land below it. ## Context The tab nav (`.docs-component-viewer-tabbed-content.docs-sticky-top`) is `position: sticky; top: 0` inside the sidenav content, which is the scroll container. Table of contents links and fragment navigation call `scrollIntoView()`, which aligns the target with the top of that container, so the heading ends up behind the 49px tab bar. Measured on the dialog overview page at 1455x800, after clicking "Keyboard interaction" in the table of contents: | | tab nav bottom | heading top | |---|---|---| | before | 105px | 55.5px (covered) | | after | 105px | 119.5px | ## Changes - `docs/src/app/pages/component-viewer/component-viewer.scss`: `scroll-margin-top: 64px` on elements with an `id` inside `.docs-component-viewer-content`. That covers headings and example viewers on every tab of a component page. Guide pages have no sticky top bar, so they are left alone. ## Testing - `pnpm stylelint`: 0 problems. - `pnpm ng-dev format changed --check `: all files correctly formatted. - `pnpm ng-dev commit-message validate-range HEAD`: valid. - Compiled the file with the repo's `sass`. The output rule is `.docs-component-viewer-content [id] { scroll-margin-top: 64px; }`. - I did not run the Bazel docs build or `bazel test //docs/...`. Serving the docs locally needs a full Bazel build of the workspace, so the before and after were checked on the deployed site with the compiled rule injected through Playwright. ## Screenshots #### Before #### After ## Notes for reviewers - 64px is the 49px tab bar plus some breathing room. It could instead be tied to the tab height token if you prefer it derived. - The alternative is `scroll-padding-top` on `.mat-sidenav-content`. That would also offset guide pages, which have no sticky bar, so I scoped it to the component viewer. Fixes #34038

Issues.Title: feat(cdk Portal): Allow DomPortal to reference detached elements
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

There is a built-in security that blocks a detached element (one that has no parent node) to be used in a DomPortal, [here](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/265b8a48718fda931ef6c57b30b371fcd926707b/src/cdk/portal/dom-portal-outlet.ts#L145).
The only purpose of this bit of code is to ensure that _if_ the DOM node is obtained the nominal way, i.e from the component's view, then it gets put back where it was before, when the operation is done or it stops being used.

### Use Case

I have a dependency that generates DOM nodes (SVG nodes to be precise). I was using a custom directive that was using `inject(ElementRef).nativeElement` and `.replaceChildren(this.inputDOMNode())`, which works but is not great.

I discovered Portal and thought I could use it, but I actually can't because the built-in security prevents me from passing a detached element to DOMPortal(). I guess I could instanciate a dummy DOM node (itself detached) to attach all my SVG nodes to it before passing them to the DOMPortal, but that's nonsense really, I just don't need the housekeeping feature of placing the node back where it was found.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "feat(cdk Portal): Allow DomPortal to reference detached elements" (#34023)

Issues.Title: feat(Paginator): Fix the default "1 – 10 of 100" syntax
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

By default, [Paginator](https://material.angular.dev/components/paginator/overview) shows text like "1 – 10 of 100". The space around the en-dash is incorrect syntax. There is no style guide that uses that. Even British style guides, e.g., [New Hart's Rules: The Oxford Style Guide](https://oceanide.es/losarchivos/docs/new-harts-rules-2005.pdf), which use spaces around en-dashes in some situations, don't use it for ranges.

The correct text should be "1–10 of 100".

### Use Case

While this can be replaced through `MatPaginatorIntl`, the default English label should also be correct for projects that do not need i18n. I know this is a "breaking change" as it might break screenshot and text-based tests, but it can be done for a major release.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "feat(Paginator): Fix the default "1 – 10 of 100" syntax" (#34021)
